D1.notes: Idea A (standing frame on the rail front, Y 10 to 14, bosses to Y 17.5) built and studied for 9 N pull and push. Reaction 9.00 N. Surface sz at the side-bar root 4.76 MPa against hand 4.77. Max displacement 1.94 mm against hand 1.06 mm (1.8 times; the top bar also bends, not checked further). Sharp opening corners are singular (8.99 MPa at 1.5 mm, 10.25 at 1.0), so R1 fillets were added in a copy: 10.67 and 10.75 MPa, 0.8 % apart. Open area 48.7 % with the rail behind the board counted (fails 50 %), 58.5 % without. Front components are limited to 5.9 mm by the Y 25 envelope, so the 14 mm allowance is not met. M3 pilot holes and inserts in the bosses are not modelled.

fasteners.type: M3 screw through board hole into boss
fasteners.reach: from the board front with a 2.5 mm hex

fasteners.type: M5 x 20 with T-nut in rail front T-slot, through bottom bar Ø5.5
fasteners.reach: behind the board, reached only after the board is off

board_removal_steps: Unplug the two 4 mm2 pairs at the 60 mm wire edge (X +42.5).
With a 2.5 mm hex from the front, remove the four M3 screws in the board holes.
Pull the board forward (+Y) off the four bosses. The mount and its M5 screws stay on the rail.
D1.governing: In-plane bending at the R1 fillet where the side bar meets the bottom bar on the rail face (10.7 MPa, 9 N pull)
D1.print_orientation: Mount lying flat on the bed (Y up, layers in XZ), bosses up, no supports; one piece
assumptions: Board stands in the XZ plane (only orientation that fits Y ±25)
Envelope applies to the mount, not the board
Rail rigid, bears on the two M5 screws
Board holes Ø3.2 at X ±39, Z -13.5 and 39.5
9 N as 2.25 N per boss, pull and push cases
questions: Does the Y ±25 envelope include the board and its components? (assumed: no)
Is the 14 mm front clearance a hard need? (assumed: no, 5.9 mm)
Does a rail 7.5 mm behind the board count against open area? (assumed: yes)
Is M3 access from the front enough? (assumed: yes)
ideas_tried: A: standing frame on the rail front (built)
B: horizontal cradle on top of the rail (picture only; the 60 mm board across Y breaks the envelope by 5 mm each side)

D2.notes: Two halves and the ring built and checked: volumes match hand, no feature errors, STL and picture sheets made. NOT DONE: no contact study for either load case, no screw load from a study, contact not proved. The brief needs ring-to-seat and half-to-half contact, which is a multi-body model with clearances and screws, not attempted in the time left. The design also does not clamp the ring radially (S6).
spec_problems: S1 screws at X ±28.2: wall from Ø3.4 hole to seat 0.5 mm (0.2 mm for the Ø4.0 insert). Built at X ±30: 2.5 and 2.2 mm
S2 seat Ø52.0 equals ring OD 52.0: zero fit, and ±0.15 mm printing gives loose or too tight. Built Ø51.6: 0.4 mm diametral interference
S3 shoulder opening Ø43.5 is smaller than the inner ring OD 44.0: rubs the turning inner ring on its end face. Built Ø44.4: 0.2 mm clear
S4 split gap not given. Built 0.4 mm (0.2 each half)
S5 screws at Z 1 and 6 are 5 mm apart with Ø6 counterbores: 1 mm overlap, and SolidWorks refuses the cut. Built Z 0.5 and 7.5 (1 mm web)

S6 clamp: Y-screws closing a 0.4 mm split on a concentric seat change its radius by about 0.0008 mm (hand: d²/8R, d/2 = 0.2, R = 25.8). The halves do not squeeze the ring; it is held by interference only. Not fixed: needs an offset (pinched) seat, not tested
D2.fit_reasoning: Ring OD 52.0 into seat 51.6 is 0.2 mm radial interference per side. Printing ±0.15 mm on the seat gives an interference of 0.25 to 0.55 mm diametral, so the ring is pressed in. The Y screws do not clamp it radially (S6).
D2.hand_screw_load_note: 300 N along +Y: four screws in tension, 75 N each. 300 N along +X: 75 N shear each (no friction).
D2.print_orientation: Each half printed with the bearing axis Z up (layers in XY, so screw and bearing loads act in-layer). The seat ledge at Z 7 is a 3.6 mm radial overhang: needs support inside the seat.
D2.why: No contact study run and no load result. The design does not clamp the ring radially (S6).

D3.notes: Part one: one script built P1 to P6 from the table. Each feature checked against its hand volume; STL watertight and one body, STL volume within 0.2 % of the part. Part two: the saved parts were opened and edited (base depth, counterbore depth, chamfer; P3 ring A sketch redrawn) and saved as _b. Feature trees before and after match except the added chamfer. Table problems were found before building; every changed row is in plates[].why.

table_problems: Column "on circle Ø" is a pitch-circle diameter. Read as radius, every hole lands outside the plate. Built with R = Ø/2.
P1: ring A (Ø3.4 on R25, 0 deg) and ring B counterbore (Ø8 on R30, 0 deg) overlap by 0.7 mm. Ring B turned 45 deg (min wall 1.0 mm).
P2: ring A and ring B are identical (6 x Ø4.5 on Ø62, both 0 deg): duplicate holes. Ring B turned 30 deg.
P4: ring B holes and counterbores at R29 break out of OD 60 by 3.0 mm. OD raised to 68 (1.0 mm wall at the counterbore).
P4: counterbore 8 x 4.6 in a 5 mm plate leaves a 0.4 mm floor, below the 0.6 mm wall rule. Depth set to 4.0 (floor 1.0 mm).
P1, P3, P4: a 1.0 mm wall at the counterbore spots, so a 1.0 mm chamfer leaves no flat. Chamfer 0.5 mm there, 1.0 mm elsewhere.
P3 part two: ring A on R35 at 0 deg leaves a 0.3 mm web to the ring B counterbore (Ø10 at R42). Turned 22.5 deg: min web 1.0 mm.
D3.edited_not_rebuilt_evidence: Part two opens each saved P*.SLDPRT and changes the BASE depth and CB depth with set_dim, redraws HA_SK for P3 with redraw_circles. Feature trees before and after match, plus TOP_CH. Nothing is rebuilt from the script.
